text:
kai: proposing a new 'quarantine + hot-swap' flow for flaky GPU nodes to avoid full drains when possible. idea: on ECC/Xid burst -> mark node QUARANTINE, probe ephemeral eviction of affected GPU device, attempt live remap (or migrate pods off GPU instance) for up to 10m; if repeated failures, escalate to CORDON+DRAIN. keeps SLOs while reducing churn. thoughts?

maria: love this. can we rely on existing metrics? we already emit `nvidia.xid_rate` and `gpu_ecc_errors` from health-agent. we should also correlate with job retry counts so we don't swap for noisy jobs. :+1:

sam: question: how do we do the "hot-swap" in k8s + slurm worlds? we don't have MIG on a lot of cards. is the plan to evict pods that reference that GPU PCI id and rebind them to another node?

kai: good Q. two approaches depending on env: 
1) k8s: attach a node-level device fence controller that can remove a single GPU from the schedulable pool (taint the device, not the node), then use pod preemption + node-affinity to migrate. example taint: `kubectl taint nodes node-123 gpu-device-1=quarantine:NoSchedule --overwrite`. the controller would maintain lists of device-level allocs.
2) slurm: set GRES unhealthy for that GPU and let prolog/epilog reschedule. `scontrol update NodeName=node-123 GRES=gres/gpu:0`.

maria: hmm, we need infra-side support: health-agent must expose `device_id` in the event. current exporter only tags node-level. i'll open a tiny patch.

nate: what about the detection rules? i've seen noisy Xid bursts during noisy neighbors (PCI hiccups). propose debounce: `if xid_count >= 6 within 3m AND avg_temp < 85C AND job_restart_rate < 2% => quarantine probe` else immediate cordon.

anne: +1 to debounce. also add a probation window: quarantine period 15m, if we observe no new Xid then clear automatically. if repeated quarantines (3 in 24h) -> mark for hardware replacement.

sam: what about job SLOs? we should prefer probe that migrates non-latency critical jobs first. can we add priority tiers in the controller?

kai: yes — controller should consult node labels + pod annotations `redwood/infer-slo=low|high` and pick low-slo pods first. fallback: if no low-slo pods, do a graceful partial-evict with max disruption cap per zone.

maria: ops question: what command will an oncall run to force swap or bypass? pls include simple CLI.

kai: CLI examples: 
```
# mark device 1 as quarantined
rdctl node quarantine --node node-123 --device-id pci:0000:af:00.1 --reason xid-burst
# force hard drain
rdctl node cordon --node node-123 --force
```

nate: log match for Xid in exporter: `dmesg | grep -E "NVRM: Xid \d+:"` or better, our agent uses `journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver | grep Xid`. sample regex we added in the patch: `NVRM: Xid (\d+): .*GPU (\S+):`.

dev-bot: automated-check: rollout of quarantine-controller v0.3 started to canary cluster alpha-zone-2 (job id: deploy-3342).

anne: runbook notes: ensure runbook covers cross-region capacity check before swapping – don't trigger device-level quarantine if zone only has 1 available spare and we risk failure to schedule. also record cost impact metric `swap_relocation_token_cost` for billing analysis.

kai: action items i will take: 1) PR to health-agent to include pci id + xid_count aggregation (maria volunteered); 2) spike quarantine-controller design (probation: 15m, tries: 2, replacement threshold: 3 in 24h); 3) runbook + rdctl docs. i'll open tickets and a short RFC.

maria: i'll drop the exporter patch today and add the `device_id` field.

sam: if you want i can prototype k8s device fence code next sprint.

kai: sweet. aim to test in alpha-zone-2 canary next week. thanks all. :rocket:
